guide.description: sed 's/pattern/replacement/' rewrites matching text on every line. By default it only replaces the FIRST match per line — add a trailing g (global) to replace every match on the line instead. Matching is case-sensitive, just like grep.

flags.desc: (inside the expression, not a real flag) replace every match per line, not just the first

examples.output:
200 GET /home
404 GET /miSsing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/uSers
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page
examples.note: only the FIRST s on a line is replaced

examples.output:
200 GET /home
404 GET /miSSing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/uSerS
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page
examples.note: g catches every s on the line

exercises.title: sed's first-match default
exercises.task: Replace the first lowercase 's' on every line of access.log with 'S'.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: sed 's/from/to/' <file> replaces only the FIRST match per line
The letter to replace is a lowercase s, swapped for an uppercase S

criteria.label: Replace only the first s per line

check.expected:
200 GET /home
404 GET /miSsing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/uSers
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

exercises.expectedOutput:
200 GET /home
404 GET /miSsing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/uSers
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

exercises.title: Global replace with g
exercises.task: Same substitution, but this time replace EVERY lowercase 's' on each line, not just the first, using the g suffix. Notice 'missing' and 'users' each have two.

hints: Add g right after the closing slash to replace every match, not just the first
